title: POC weekly sync - rollout / go-live planning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on rollout and go-live planning. Reviewed canary/cutover approach, monitoring and runbook items, gating criteria, and next steps: dry-run, runbook draft, pricing/SLA confirmation, and staging access. Discussed fallback model variants, latency targets, and security checklist (SOC2/KMS).
topics: Next steps: dry run and SLA/pricing

Liam (Redwood SE) - Share runbook draft and canary playbook in docs redwood link by 2026-04-05

transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-04-01 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 50m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE); Jordan Patel (Redwood CSM); Evan Brooks (Atlas CTO); Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng); Marco Rivas (Infra); Sofia Lee (Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes today. quick agenda, go-live planning, canary strategy, monitoring, runbooks, security gating. Evan over to you, any agenda additions?
[00:12] Evan: No, that sounds perfect. we want to make sure the cutover is low risk, minimize customer impact, and have clear fallback.
[00:20] Priya: Also want to align on performance targets — p95 latency under 450ms and error rate under 0.5% during canary. those are our internal targets.
[00:30] Liam: Great, we can work to hit that. from the POC we've seen median latency around 220ms on hosted, but tail can spike with longer sequences, and with your batch patterns we should tune continuous batching and KV cache hit rates.
[00:42] Marco: Quick network note — for Redwood Private we'll need a VPC peering and a couple of firewall ports opened, I'll share the exact CIDR and ports after.
[00:51] Maya: Thanks Marco. ok canary approach suggestion: 10% traffic for 24 hours, monitor SLOs (p95 latency, error rate, token cost), then 50% for 6 hours if green, then 100% cutover overnight with rollback window. We also recommend an A/B variant test for model quality — route 10% to quantized variant + 90% to baseline to check quality regressions.
[01:12] Priya: A/B for quantized variant sounds good, but we need an automated quality check. can we attach a small eval set and run online evals during canary?
[01:21] Liam: Yes, we can wire up a sentinel eval set that runs every 1000 requests or so and flags drift beyond a threshold. also Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles based on tokens/sec and quality loss tradeoff.
[01:33] Sofia: Also need to confirm how to surface alerts to our pager — we use PagerDuty.
[01:38] Jordan: We have PagerDuty integrations — we'll configure a new service and map alerts for p95 and error-rate thresholds, plus a separate alert for model quality regressions.
[01:46] Evan: On rollback criteria, what's a good cut? like if p95 > 700ms or error rate > 1% we rollback?
[01:52] Liam: That seems reasonable. I'd suggest two-tier: soft threshold for on-call awareness (p95 > 500ms or error rate > 0.5%) and hard threshold for automatic rollback (p95 > 700ms or error rate > 1.0% for > 5 minutes). We can set that in the routing policy.
[02:12] Priya: Sounds fair. Regarding data retention during POC, we need to be sure logs aren't persisted beyond 30 days unless encrypted and approved. do you have KMS integration?
[02:21] Maya: Yes, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS/HSM for private deployments. we'll share the KMS integration guide. (mumbles) oh sometimes the docs says Redwood Privet — it's Redwood Private.
[02:34] Evan: [laughs] we've seen that in the transcript, it's fine. security-wise we also need SOC2 and ISO references for our compliance team.
[02:41] Jordan: I'll attach our SOC2 Type II report and the summary notes.
[02:45] Marco: For network dry-run, we'd like to do a simulated traffic replay from staging that mirrors production 1% slice. can Redwood handle prefix caching warm-up?
[02:54] Liam: Yes — we support prefix/K-V caching (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash) and we can pre-warm caches during the dry-run. we can also do controlled ramping to warm the KV cache before canary starts.
[03:10] Sofia: About rollout timing — we prefer a 2am local cutover window to minimize user impact, but will rely on the staging dry-run to pick exact timing.
[03:17] Maya: Good. let's talk about runbook ownership. Liam, Jordan — will own runbook authoring from Redwood side; Priya and Marco will own Atlas validation. runbook items should include pre-cutover checks, canary monitoring dashboard links, automatic rollback steps, and post-cutover verification collection.
[03:34] Liam: I'll draft the runbook and include a playbook for canary -> increase -> rollback including commands for route changes and model pinning. note: pinning model versions is supported in the control plane.
[03:44] Priya: On visibility, we need token-level cost breakdown for the canary so finance can see projected rollout spend.
[03:50] Maya: We'll provide a forecast export and a per-route cost dashboard.
[03:55] Evan: One more question on fallbacks — if Dedicated capacity hits saturation, can we fallback to hosted without tokenization changes?
[04:02] Liam: Yes you can. Redwood routing policy supports automatic fallback to compatible model variants in hosted tier; there are caveats around quantization differences and slight latency variance but the API remains consistent.
[04:15] Priya: For quality gating on A/B, can we configure automatic diversion if quality delta > X?
[04:21] Liam: We can surface it as an alert and optionally automate diversion. Automation requires pre-agreed thresholds and we'll include that in the runbook.
[04:30] Sofia: Do you have a suggested checklist for the dry-run?
[04:33] Maya: Yes, high level: 1) pre-cutover perf run to warm caches, 2) validate SSO and KMS connectivity, 3) run sentinel evals, 4) verify PagerDuty alerts, 5) simulate increased 10% load and observe SLOs for 2 hours, 6) test rollback in low-impact window. we'll share a checklist doc link after the call.
[04:54] Marco: On the VPC side, we'll need a maintained RDP for the peering and route table entries, and a security contact during the dry-run. I'll add that to the action items.
[05:05] Evan: OK, timeline wise can we aim for the dry-run week of 2026-04-10 and final cutover the week after if dry-run is green?
[05:13] Maya: That timeline is doable, contingent on staging access and sign off on SLA. we'll target dry-run 2026-04-10. Jordan will send a calendar invite.
[05:21] Priya: Quick point about metrics — in addition to p95 and error-rate, we want tail token generation time and token consumption per request so we can monitor cost.
[05:31] Liam: We'll include tokens/request, tokens/sec, and per-route cost in the dashboard.
[05:36] Sofia: Any procurement/package implications for Dedicated burst capacity?
[05:39] Maya: We'll send a pricing addendum — Dedicated reserved commit vs burst pricing. for the pilot we can include a small burst allowance; pricing will be in the addendum.
[05:48] Evan: For legal we need an approved DPA and export controls note. is that part of the docs you'll send?
[05:54] Jordan: Yes, we'll attach the DPA and compliance pack.
[05:58] Priya: Ok, quick technical deep-dive question — if we need to rollback to a previous model, how long does model pinning switch take? is it instant?
[06:06] Liam: In most cases the control plane can pin and switch in under 30s, but cold starts for large models can add latency for initial requests; hence warm-up is included in the runbook.
[06:18] Maya: Great. Any blockers from Atlas?
[06:21] Marco: The main blocker is getting staging network access and the traffic traces — I'll work with Priya to send both this week.
[06:27] Priya: We'll produce the traces and a 1% production slice within two days.
[06:31] Evan: Sounds good. Are there any other open security issues?
[06:34] Jordan: Not beyond the KMS and SOC2 docs, we'll follow up.
[06:38] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps — I'll send pricing + SLA by Friday, Liam will share runbook by Monday, Marco/Priya send staging access and traces, Jordan schedules the dry-run for 2026-04-10.
[06:52] Evan: Works for us.
[06:55] Maya: Thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after the dry-run for an after-action review.
[06:59] [call ends]

Notes: Transcription contains occasional word swaps ("Privet" for Private, "K-V cash" for KV cache). Natural speech patterns present. Links referenced: runbook draft (link to be shared), SOC2 pdf (attached by Jordan), pricing addendum (to be attached by Maya).
notes: Call included typical sales + SE presence; strong focus on operational rollouts and safety. There was talk of A/B tests, automatic rollback, canary duration and thresholds. Redwood to provide runbook and pricing. Atlas to provide staging artifacts.
